citations.desc: Institutional Animal Care and Use Committee (IACUC).
citations.narrative:
A study-related sedation and procedure were intended to be performed on a pig covered under research protocol
20XXXXXX42 on September 16, 2024. However, a pig covered under research protocol 20XXXXXXX44 was mistakenly
sedated on this day instead of the intended animal. The animal was administered reversal of the sedation when the error
was identified and recovered uneventfully, according to the facility veterinarian.
Sedation for a procedure approved under a different protocol from the one intended constitutes a deviation from the
approved activities on the protocol.
This incident was reported in the IACUC meeting minutes and corrective measures, including verifying that animals are
covered under the correct protocol and properly identified, were implemented prior to the inspection.

citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care.
citations.narrative:
An approximately 3-month-old female guinea pig was transported to the facility on December 1, 2025. Between
December 1, 2025, and December 8, 2025, the animal lost 130 grams, or 22.9% of its weight on arrival. Veterinary and
laboratory personnel did not observe abnormal behaviors in this timeframe.
A study experiment was performed on December 9, 2025, and the animal was found deceased on December 10, 2025.
Despite the significant weight reduction in this animal measured by laboratory personnel, there was no communication to
the facility veterinarian prior to performing study activities on this animal.
Significant weight reduction in a short amount of time is highly suggestive of an underlying disease and can be associated
with pain or distress in animals.
The facility shall establish and maintain programs of adequate veterinary care including mechanisms of direct and
frequent communication so that timely and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is
conveyed to the Attending Veterinarian.
The facility implemented corrective measures, including a review of signs of health, pain, and body condition scoring of
this species, prior to the inspection. To remain corrected from June 3, 2026, forward.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
